main_reasons: NAHD merger paid in convertible preferred (4M shares convertible 1:15, roughly 90% of post-conversion common), done to meet the Nasdaq equity rule. The target's CEO (McLaren, a related-party noteholder) became the company's CEO, so this looks like a reverse acquisition that was booked as a forward acquisition

$15.6M goodwill (vs $3.2M net assets acquired; NAHD contributed $0.67M revenue and a $1.77M loss) and $17.4M total goodwill make up about half of total assets. Equity is only +$7.6M, so without this goodwill the company would have a stockholders' deficit

Goodwill impairment test was qualitative only and found no impairment, despite going concern doubt, a gross loss, a full-cost ceiling write-down, a collapsing share price, Machfu employee terminations and lawsuits, and SG Echo's Chapter 11 filing. The test also cites a 'stockholders' deficit' that does not match the reported positive equity

Large Level 3 fair values drive the numbers: preferred valued at $18.8M, intangibles, and oil and gas reserves. Derivative losses and gains of several million dollars on notes of only a few hundred thousand dollars produce big swings in earnings
Auditor M&K resigned in January 2026, and new auditor RBSM issued a first-year opinion. The 10-K was filed late (around June 30, 2026) and the registrant checked 'No' on timely filing of all reports
Material weaknesses in the close process and in technical accounting, with numerous year-end auditor adjustments

Many internal inconsistencies: MD&A labels the $4.75M other expense as income, cash and operating cash flow figures differ between sections, a related-party debt forgiveness was booked to APIC, a $311,560 SG DevCorp loss is disclosed but missing from the income statement, and a $2.0M legal settlement gain does not reconcile with $975,784 of proceeds in cash flows

Severe financial distress: $0.43M cash, $24.3M working-capital deficit, toxic convertible notes and merchant cash advances, repeated reverse splits, and serial acquisitions paid with stock and notes (including a $30M CS Digital deal after year end)
